reading.title: Engineering case — Test a crash point rather than a convenient outage
paragraphs: A test stops the worker before the gateway sends a request. The gateway later retries and succeeds. This is useful evidence for dependency unavailability, but it does not test duplicate safety after a committed effect.

Move the failpoint to the interval after the worker’s transaction commits and before the reply is delivered. Now the gateway cannot distinguish completed work from failed delivery using the connection alone. The test must verify a later retry returns the retained result and that the receipt count remains one.

The worker’s drop-first-reply option creates exactly that history. It does not crash the process, so receipt persistence across process replacement is a separate test. Combining both ideas into one oversized test could make failures harder to diagnose. Separate cases isolate the mechanism under examination while the complete suite covers their composition more broadly.

An independent oracle should inspect the authoritative effect count and result, not merely accept the gateway’s final success message. If both the worker and gateway contained the same duplicate-counting bug, a response-only test could miss it. The integration suite queries the worker count and verifies status values.

The test harness uses ephemeral ports and waits for a specific startup line instead of sleeping for an arbitrary duration. It also bounds every wait and cleans up processes on failure. A test that hangs indefinitely or leaks a server into later tests can create misleading failures unrelated to the intended invariant.

Record the first failing history and preserve relevant stderr. Sanitizer output should not disappear because a cleanup helper catches every exception. Conversely, a normal process signal during an intentional test should not automatically be classified as an application defect. The harness must understand the expected termination path.

The general pattern is to name the failpoint relative to a commit, publication, or ownership transfer. “Make it fail sometimes” is much less useful than “lose the acknowledgement after the durable effect and before local completion.” Precise placement turns failure injection into evidence rather than noise.
